cards.explanation: The answer is Moses, friends. The Levite heads say it plainly: "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given cities in which to live…" (Joshua 21:2). They aren't asking for a favor here. They're holding up a command that was already given, like walking into the bakery with the receipt in hand.

The answer is cities to live in! The Levite heads say the LORD commanded "…that we be given cities in which to live…" (Joshua 21:2). Pasturelands for their livestock come along with them. Forty-eight cities by the end (Joshua 21:41). FORTY-EIGHT. Somebody is going to need a very long list of housewarming parties, friends.

The answer is pasturelands. The Levite heads ask for cities "…together with pasturelands for our livestock." (Joshua 21:2). Animals need grass, and grass needs room. Even I know you can't keep a herd in a cookie jar.

The answer is that they give cities out of their own land, friends. The text says the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and pasturelands "…out of their own inheritance…" (Joshua 21:3). Think about that. Giving up a piece of your own land is like handing over the corner pieces of a fresh batch and saying, "Take the good ones." They did it "…by the command of the LORD…" and gave from what was already theirs.
The answer is all of it, friends. The text says, "Thus the LORD gave Israel all the land He had sworn to give their fathers…" (Joshua 21:43). Not a piece of it, not most of it. All of it.

The answer is True. The verse says Israel "…took possession of it and settled in it." (Joshua 21:43). They got the land, and then they unpacked. That's a good feeling for any family, after all the moving around.

The answer is rest. "And the LORD gave them rest on every side, just as He had sworn to their fathers." (Joshua 21:44). On every side, friends. That's the kind of rest I dream about after a full day of stamping.

The answer is that the LORD handed them all over to Israel. The verse says, "…the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand." (Joshua 21:44). So none of them could stand against Israel. The credit goes to the LORD.

The answer is False. The verse says, "Not one of all the LORD’s good promises to the house of Israel had failed; everything was fulfilled." (Joshua 21:45). Not one, friends. I've had a lot of cookie batches fall apart on me, so a record like that is something.
